newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MUI not seeking further acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: MUI not seeking further acquisitions.

text.p: Malayan United Industries Bhd (MUI) said on Friday that it was not planning any further acquisitions for the time being, but that any further purchases it makes will fit within its current businesses.

"We are currently in the areas of cement, media, property and construction, hotels, both local and overseas," Ng Kwan Cheong, group managing director of MUI said at a press conference on Friday following the company's extraordinary general meeting.
"These are areas that we are in and will try to enhance further. Our priority is shareholder value. Any acquisitions we make will have to be synergistic with current operations," he added.

Diversified MUI recently won control of multi-industry concern Pengkalen Holdings Bhd, which has interests in two stockbroking companies via its Pengkalen Capital Bhd unit following a well-publicised takeover battle that included a fight for boardroom seats.
In August, MUI appointed its own slate of directors to Pengkalen Holdings after its successful acquisition of a controlling stake at 4.04 to 6.20 ringgit a share.
Discussing the outlook for Pengkalen, Ng said: "We have long-term expectations that Pengkalen will be a major contributor to group profit." He did not give details.
MUI officials said Pengkalen could be profitable by the next financial year. The company posted a loss of 9.88 million ringgit, or 27.50 cents a share, for the financial year ended in March 1996.
